text: Henry Nolan’s motive to evoke nostalgia and a sense of belonging is structurally reinforced through the use of the old mill as a central metaphor. By positioning the mill as a symbol of stability and resistance against modernity, the author aligns the thematic structure of tradition and community with his intent to critique the rapid changes of the contemporary world. This structural choice ensures that the setting itself drives the narrative’s emotional resonance, linking the physical permanence of the mill to the enduring value of communal ties.
